$comment: The cross-language contract for the settings layer — doc 15 §1.4 test 6.
Two implementations of one resolver (TypeScript in ingestion-service, Python
in rag-service) is the same class of duplication as the quota key and the
purpose enums (13-doc §1.1), and it drifts the same way: someone retunes
finalContextK on one side, both services keep working, and the two halves of
a single AI request now disagree about how much context an answer gets.
This file is NOT read at runtime by either service, and that is deliberate.
Loading shared JSON from disk would make a Python container's boot depend on
a path inside a TypeScript library — a packaging problem traded for a
correctness one. Instead both sides hold their own literals and both test
suites assert equality against this file, so a change on either side that is
not made on the other fails that side's own tests, in that side's own CI job.
Changing a default therefore means editing three files. That friction is the
feature: it is exactly one file more than the number of places the value has
